```{r dataset}
#%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%#######-##-
##### Import and clean the raw survey database %%%%%%%%%%%##
#####%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%#######-###-

##Import data_full, the baseline dataset
data_full <- read_csv("../Data/BaselinePremiersPas.csv")


##Import data_tot_clean with excluded participants (the ones that were undocumented or did not leave their phone number)
data_tot_clean <- read_csv("../Data/Full_dataset_PremiersPas_with_undocumented.csv") 



#convert relevant VARIABLES INTO FACTORS
##NB: pour ajouter les stats sur les heures, prendre le dataset du 24/10 et ajouter "'HOUR_1','HOUR_2','HOUR_3','HOUR_4',"
names <- c("ResponseId", "SurveyorId", "MaternityWard", "Dep", "CodePostal", "DateArrival",
           "DateArrival2", "SansPapier", "Relationship", "Language", "Preg7Less", "SmokePreg", 
           "BreastFeedIntend", "OrderedEduc", "Educ", "Act3", "FmlyIncome", "Income", "ECSType7", "FrenchYN", 
           "Intention.x", "ECSUsed", "ECSNeed", "ECSIdealAgeEntry", "AffordSubsidies", "AffordNMCostWB", "AffordOppCost", 
           "AffordNMCostCareer", "DiscountRate", "AccessEasy", "AccessHours", "AccessInformalCare", "Norms", "NormsOpposedDK",
           "LikertAccessInfo", "LikertReturnHK", "LikertAccessSoc", "TrustFam", "TrustFriend", "TrustAssMat", "TrustCreche", 
           "DeprivClothes", "DeprivFood", "DeprivBills", "DeprivHolidays", "DeprivHousing", "InformalReciprocity", 
           "LevelComprehensionExPost", "LevelExpressionExPost", "LevelInfoSubExPost", "LevelPartnerAnsweredExPost", 
           "ComputerYN", "AgeSup32", "BirthPlace", "BirthPlace2", "OrderedEduc2", "Occupation", "Occupation2",

           "Assignment", "Which_wave", "labels", "blocksMatWaveStrata", "blocksMatWave", "code_commune", "code_departement"
           
)

data_full[,names] <- lapply(data_full[,names] , factor)

#convert relevant VARIABLES INTO numerical ones


names_numerical <- c("AgeChild1", "AgeChild2", "AgeChild3", "AgeChild4", "AgeChild5", "AgeChild6", "AgeChild7", "AgeChild8",
                     "Age", "KnowsCreche", "KnowsCrecheA", "KnowsCrechePub", "KnowsAssMat", "KnowsNotYet", "KnowsJE", "KnowsAutre",
                     "KnowsPartage", "KnowsHG", "KnowsNounou", "KnowsNothing", "WantCreche", "WantCrecheA", "WantAssMat", "WantJE", 
                     "WantAutre", "WantPartage", "WantHG", "WantNounou", "KnownNbTypeECS", "PregMonth", "BreastFeedLength",
                     "BreastFeedIntend1or0", "AffordSubsidies1or0", "NormsOpposedN", "LikertReturnHK1or0", "TrustCreche1or0",
                     "AffordCost", "NumberChildren", "AccessImpossible", "AccessHard", "AccessHardtoImpossible", "AccessEasy1or0", 
                     "AccessEasyDK", "AccessNotHours", "AccessNotInformalCare", "AccessInformalCareAMAP", "ValGenerosity", 
                     "ValIndependence", "ValSocialisation", "ValObedience", "ValEducation", "ValDK", "ValImagination", "ValNone", 
                     "WorkBefore", "FmilyEarnLessThan2500", "EarnLessThan1500", "Intention1or0", "CODDEP", "CODREG", "PTOT", 
                     "TAUXCOUV_COM", "TAUXCOUV_EPCI", "TAUXCOUV_DEP", "TAUXCOUV_NAT", "n", "strata", "group_id", "prixMoyen", 
                     "PrixMedian", "surfaceReelleBati", "PrixMoyenM2Bati")
data_full[,names_numerical] <- lapply(data_full[,names_numerical] , as.numeric)

# Order relevant variables


data_full <- data_full %>%  mutate(
         OrderedEduc=factor(OrderedEduc, levels =
             c("No school", "9-11", "Brevet", "CAP", "Bac", "Bac +2", "Bac + 3", "Bac + 4/5", "+ Bac+5"), ordered = TRUE),
         Income = factor(Income, 
                         levels = c("NSP","- 500","500-700", "1000-1500", 
                                    "1500-2000", "2000-2500", "2500-3000", "3000-4500", "4500-5000",  "5000-6000", "Ne veut pas répondre" ), ordered = TRUE),
         FmlyIncome = factor(FmlyIncome, 
                             levels =c("NSP", "- 500", "500-700", "700-1000", "1000-1500", 
                                       "1500-2000", "2000-2500", "2500-3000", "3000-4500", "4500-5000",
                                       "5000-6000", "6000-7000", "7000-8000", "+8000", "Ne veut pas répondre"), ordered = TRUE),
          AffordNMCostWBOrdered=factor(AffordNMCostWB,

         AffordOppCost=factor(AffordOppCost,
                              levels=c("Négatif",  "Je ne sais pas encore", "Pas d'impact", "Positif"), ordered = TRUE # would staying at home have a positive, 
         ),                                                                   # negative or null impact on household's income
         AffordNMCostCareer=factor(AffordNMCostCareer, # would staying at home have a positive, 
                                   levels=c("Négatif", "Pas d'impact", "Je ne sais pas encore","Positif"), ordered = TRUE # negative or null impact on mother's career
         ),
         AccessEasy=factor(AccessEasy,levels =c("impossible","quasiment impossible", # Whether accessing a slot in ECS is seen as easy
                                                   "très difficile","assez difficile",
                                                   "je ne sais pas","assez facile",
                                                   "très facile"),ordered = TRUE), 
         AccessHours=factor(AccessHours,levels =c("Oui", # Whether ECS opening hours fit parents working hours
                                                     "Non, mais on prendra un autre mode de garde en plus","Je ne sais pas encore",
                                                     "Non"),ordered = TRUE),
         AccessInformalCare=factor(AccessInformalCare,levels =c("Oui, autant que nécessaire", # Whether accessing informal care is feasible
                                                          "Oui, de temps en temps","Oui, pour dépanner / très ponctuellement",
                                                          "Je ne sais pas encore",
                                                          "Non"),ordered = TRUE),
         Norms=factor(Norms,
                      levels=c("Ne sait pas","Aucune","Une minorité","Moitié moitié","La plupart","Toutes"), ordered = TRUE # how many mothers in their surroundings use childcare 
         ),
     LikertAccessInfo=factor(LikertAccessInfo, # Is it feasible to access information about childcare
                            levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord"), ordered = TRUE), # strongly disagree, disagree, don't know, agree, strongly agree
    LikertReturnHK=factor(LikertReturnHK, # believe in childcare returns on investment: is a child that attended childcare better developed in preschool?
                          levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord") , ordered = TRUE), # strongly disagree, disagree, don't know, agree, strongly agree
    LikertAccessSoc=factor(LikertAccessSoc, # Does the mother have someone that can help with paperwork if needed
                           levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord"), ordered = TRUE), # strongly disagree, disagree, don't know, agree, strongly agree
    TrustFam=factor(TrustFam, # TRUST: Do the parents trust their close family (parents, brother, sister, etc.) to take care of the baby
                    levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord"),  ordered = TRUE
    ),
    TrustFriend=factor(TrustFriend, # TRUST: Do the parents trust their friends to take care of the baby
                       levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord"), ordered = TRUE
    ),
    TrustAssMat=factor(TrustAssMat, # TRUST: Do the parents trust a private childminder to take care of the baby
                       levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord"), ordered = TRUE
    ),
    TrustCreche=factor(TrustCreche, # TRUST: Do the parents trust their family to take care of the baby
                       levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord"), ordered = TRUE
    ),
    DeprivClothes =factor(DeprivClothes,levels=c("Pas du tout","Un peu","Beaucoup","Je ne souhaite pas répondre"), ordered = TRUE), # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to buy clothes?
    DeprivFood    =factor(DeprivFood,levels=c("Pas du tout","Un peu","Beaucoup","Je ne souhaite pas répondre"), ordered = TRUE), # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to buy food?
    DeprivBills   =factor(DeprivBills,levels=c("Pas du tout","Un peu","Beaucoup","Je ne souhaite pas répondre"), ordered = TRUE), # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to pay for the bills?
    DeprivHolidays=factor(DeprivHolidays,levels=c("Pas du tout","Un peu","Beaucoup","Je ne souhaite pas répondre"), ordered = TRUE), # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to go in holidays?
    DeprivHousing =factor(DeprivHousing,levels=c("Pas du tout","Un peu","Beaucoup","Je ne souhaite pas répondre"), ordered = TRUE), # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to pay for housing?
    InformalReciprocity = factor(InformalReciprocity, 
                                 levels = c( "Non", " Je ne souhaite pas répondre", "Oui, pour dépanner / très ponctuellement",
                                              "Oui, de temps en temps", " Oui, très souvent"), ordered = TRUE), # Do the parents already take care of the children of others
OrderedEduc2=factor(OrderedEduc2, levels  = c(
  "No school", "9-11", "Brevet", "CAP", "Bac", "Bac +2", "Bac + 3", "Bac + 4/5", "+ Bac+5","Missing","No Partner"), ordered = TRUE),
ECSIdealAgeEntry = factor(ECSIdealAgeEntry,

Active = ifelse(as.character(Act3) == "NSP", "Inactive", as.character(Act3)), 
Active = relevel(as.factor(Active), ref = "Inactive"), 
Active1or0 = ifelse(as.character(Active) == "Inactive", 0, 1),
Educ3 = fct_collapse(OrderedEduc, "Bac or Less" = c("No school", "9-11", "Brevet", "CAP", "Bac"),

Educ3Dad = fct_collapse(OrderedEduc2, "Bac or Less" = c("No school", "9-11", "Brevet", "CAP", "Bac"),

Intention1or0 = ifelse(as.character(Intention.x) == "No", 0, 1)

)
```

# Part {-}: Brief description of the sample

This first part is dedicated to a description of the sample.

## Main characteristics of the dataset

### Total sample

`r data_tot_clean %>% nrow()` surveys have been completed overall. Responses with no contact information or from undocumented mothers were excluded, for ethical reasons for the latter.

## Brief description of the participants included

Over the `r data_full %>% nrow()` remaining participants,

-   `r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow()/data_full %>% nrow()*100, digit = 2)` % are Low-SES (i.e., no tertiary education) (N=`r data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow()`).

-   `r round(data_full %>% filter(ECSUsed == "Non") %>% nrow()/data_full %>% nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % have never used ECS (N=`r data_full %>% filter(ECSUsed == "Non") %>% nrow()`)

-   Single mothers: `r round(data_full %>% filter(SingleMum == TRUE) %>% nrow()/data_full %>% nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % (N =`r data_full %>% filter(SingleMum == TRUE) %>% nrow()`). Mothers were recruited between their fourth and ninth months of pregnancy.

-   Primparae: `r round(data_full %>% filter(Primipare == TRUE) %>% nrow()/data_full %>% nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % (N =`r data_full %>% filter(Primipare == TRUE) %>% nrow()`)

-   Digital divide: More than a third (`r round((data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" & ComputerYN == "Non") %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow())*100, 1)`%) of low-SES respondents don't have access to a computer compared to `r round((data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup" & ComputerYN == "Non") %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup") %>% nrow())*100, 1)`% for High-SES respondents. Similarly, one third (`r round((data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else" & ComputerYN == "Non") %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else") %>% nrow())*100, 1)`%) of mothers born abroad don't have access to a computer compared to `r round((data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "French" & ComputerYN == "Non") %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "French") %>% nrow())*100, 1)`% for non-migrants.

## Main variables

### Age

The age of the participants follows a normal distribution:

```{r Age, fig.cap= "Median and Mean Age of mothers in the sample (mean in red on the figure)"}
MeanAge = data_full %>% summarize(mean = mean(Age), median = median(Age))

regulartable(data_full %>% summarize(Mean = round(mean(Age), 1), Median = median(Age))) %>% 
  autofit()


data_full %>% 
ggplot(aes(Age))+
geom_density()+
  geom_vline(data = MeanAge, aes(xintercept=mean, color = "red"), show.legend = FALSE)+ scale_fill_discrete(guide="none")

```

### Level of education of the mothers

`r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow()/data_full %>% nrow()*100, digit = 2)` % of Low-SES (i.e., no tertiary education) (N=`r data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow()`).

```{r education, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5, fig.cap= "Distribution of the level of education of mothers in the sample"}

ggplot(data_full, aes(OrderedEduc, fill = OrderedEduc), colour = cbPalette)+

  labs( x = "Level of education of the mother")+

```

### Income range of the mothers

A significant number of mothers included in the sample earn less than 500€ per month: it is the case for `r round(data_full %>% filter(Income == "- 500") %>% nrow()/data_full %>% nrow()*100, digit = 2)` % of them. `r round(data_full %>% filter(Income == "- 500" & SingleMum == TRUE) %>% nrow()/data_full %>% nrow()*100, digit = 2)` % of the total sample earn less than 500€ per month and are single mothers.


# Part {-}: Childcare related outcomes

## Childcare plans after birth

Parents wanting to use an ECS are over-represented in the sample: `r round(data_full %>% filter(ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % want to use them.

```{r GraphMig, fig.cap= "Childcare plan after birth of mothers in the sample"}
data_full %>% 
ggplot(aes(ECSPlanTo, fill = ECSPlanTo), colour = cbPalette)+
  geom_bar()+
  scale_x_discrete(labels=c("No", "Yes"))+
  labs( x = "Want to use ECS", fill = "Want to use ECS")+scale_fill_manual(values = cbPalette, labels = c( "No", "Yes"))


```

### Analysis for low-SES

Among low-SES parents, parents wanting to use an ECS are still over-represented in the sample: `r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % want to use them compared to `r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup") %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % for the high-SES parents The same holds for migrant families: `r round(data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else") %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % want to use ECS among them. Even more interestingly, even among inactive parents, parents wanting to use an ECS are still over-represented in the sample: `r round(data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive") %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % of inactive mothers want to use ECS.

## Sensitivity analyses: robustness across several definitions of Socio-Economic Status

### Education level of the mother

Mothers with tertiary education are more likely to want ECS from about 14 percentage points.

```{r IntentionBinaryEduc, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE, fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by binary level of education of the mother"}

data_full%>%
  mutate(Intention1or0 = as.numeric(Intention1or0)) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x=Educ),position="stack",alpha=.2)+
  stat_summary(aes(x = Educ, y = Intention1or0*1000, color = Educ),
               fun.data = "mean_se",
               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975)),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
xlab("Level of education of the mother (Bac = no tertiary education)") + ylab("Pr (Intention)")+ 
  ylab("Number of observations")+
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1000, name = "Pr (Intention)"))+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle =45 , hjust = 1, vjust = 1))

```

Here is the table for three simple regression models:

1.  the first one estimates probability to intend to use ECS by mothers' level of education as a binary outcome (having a tertiary education or not).

2.  the second one is the same model, but with strata fixed effects (MaternityWardXWave)

3.  the third one is the same as 2., but controlling with a dummy for whether mothers are active (i.e. employed, student, etc.) or not.

```{r ModelEducIntention, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}


IntentionSES        <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ Educ , data = data_full) 
IntentionSESFE      <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ Educ | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~blocksMatWave) 
IntentionSESActFE   <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ Educ + Active | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~blocksMatWave)  
 

 modelsummary(list(
"Intention to use ECS by education level (dummy no tertiary education)"      = IntentionSES, 
"Intention to use ECS by education level (dummy no tertiary education) with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"      = IntentionSESFE, 
"Intention to use ECS by education level and Activity with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"      = IntentionSESActFE


), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs", "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: WardxWave"),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Intention to use ECS by Education level binary",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE)

```

There is still an effect of the level of education after controlling for whether the mother is currently active, but most of the effect of the level of education seem to go through the activity status of the mother.The R2 of the simple model with no control is quite low, but double by including mothers' activity status.

For a more fine-grained analysis, we can break down the level of education of mothers in the sample in smaller categories:

```{r graphEducDetailedIntention, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE, fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by binary level of education of the mother"}

  mutate(Intention1or0 = as.numeric(Intention1or0)) %>%

  geom_bar(aes(x=OrderedEduc),position="stack",alpha=.2)+
  stat_summary(aes(x = OrderedEduc, y = Intention1or0*1000, color = Educ),
               fun.data = "mean_se",
               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975)),

xlab("Level of education of the mother ") + ylab("Pr (Intention)")+

```

The 9-11 category's unexpected boost might be explained by the fact that these mothers are nearly exclusively from Sub-Saharan Africa and thus very favorable to ECS (see below, to be explored in more details).

### Migration background of the mother

Mothers that are born is France are slightly more likely to want ECS compared to mothers born abroad. However, the difference is very small. Interestingly, there seems to be an interaction between the level of education and the migration background of the mother that will be explored in subsequent analyses.

```{r, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE, fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by binary migration background of the mother"}


data_full%>%
  mutate(Intention1or0 = as.numeric(Intention1or0)) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x=FrenchYN),position="stack",alpha=.2)+
  stat_summary(aes(x = FrenchYN, y = Intention1or0*1000, color = Educ),
               fun.data = "mean_se",
               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975)),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
    stat_summary(aes(x = FrenchYN, y = Intention1or0*1000),
               fun.data = "mean_se",
               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975))) +
xlab("Migration background of the mother") + ylab("Pr (Intention)")+ 
  ylab("Number of observations")+
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1000, name = "Pr (Intention)"))+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle =45 , hjust = 1, vjust = 1))


```

Here is the table for first three simple regression models:

1.  the first one estimates probability to intend to use ECS by mothers' migration background as a binary outcome (being born in a French territory or not).

2.  the second one is the same model, but with strata fixed effects (MaternityWardXWave).

3.  the third model is the same as 2., but controlling for mothers' activity at the time of the interview.

```{r ModelMigIntention, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}

IntentionMig                <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ FrenchYN , data = data_full) 
IntentionMigFE              <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ FrenchYN | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~blocksMatWave) 
IntentionMigActFE              <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ FrenchYN + Active| blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~blocksMatWave) 
 

 modelsummary(list(
  "Intention to use ECS by migration background"      = IntentionMig, 
  "Intention to use ECS by migration with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"      = IntentionMigFE, 
  "Intention to use ECS by migration and activity with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"      = IntentionMigActFE

), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs", "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: WardxWave"),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Number of ECS Known (KnownNbTypeECS)",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE)

```

We can see than the difference between mothers born in France and others is very small (less than 1 percentage point), but significant. However, when we introduce mothers' activity at the time of the interview, the effect of migration background disappears. The R2 of this simple model is even smaller than the one for the level of education.

We can break down the migration background into more meaningful categories: birth regions.

```{r, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE, fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by region of origin of the mother"}

  data_full%>% filter(BirthPlace != "Je ne souhaite pas répondre" & BirthPlace != "Autre"  ) %>% 
  mutate(Intention1or0 = as.numeric(Intention1or0)) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x=BirthPlace),position="stack",alpha=.2)+
  stat_summary(aes(x = BirthPlace, y = Intention1or0*1000),
               fun.data = "mean_se",

                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
xlab("Birth region of the mother ") + ylab("Pr (Intention)")+ 
  ylab("Number of observations")+
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1000, name = "Pr (Intention)"))+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle =45 , hjust = 1, vjust = 1))+scale_x_discrete(labels=c( 'Subsaharan Afr.', 'South-America', 'Asia', "DOM-TOM", "Metr. France", "Europe", "MENA" ))

  

```

Mothers from two world regions seems to be less likely to want to use ECS: mothers from Asia and mothers from Middle East and North Africa regions (MENA).

The pattern seems quite similar if we look at fathers' region of birth instead:

### Interaction between education level and migration background of the mother.

In this paragraph, we dig deeper into the interaction between education level and migration background of the mother.

```{r, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}

IntentionEducMig    <- feols( Intention1or0 ~ Educ + FrenchYN, data = data_full) 
IntentionEducMigFE  <- feols( Intention1or0 ~ Educ + FrenchYN| blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave) 
IntentionEducMigActFE  <- feols( Intention1or0 ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Active | blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave) 
IntentionEducXMig   <- feols( Intention1or0 ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Educ*FrenchYN, data = data_full)
IntentionEducXMigFE <- feols( Intention1or0 ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Educ*FrenchYN| blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave)  
IntentionEducXMigActFE <- feols( Intention1or0 ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Active + Educ*FrenchYN| blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave)  
 

 modelsummary(list(
"Intention to use ECS by education level (dummy no tertiary education) and migration background of the mother" = IntentionEducMig, 
"Intention to use ECS by education level (dummy no tertiary education) and migration background of the mother with FE"= IntentionEducMigFE,
"Intention to use ECS by education level (dummy no tertiary education) and migration background of the mother controlling for activity with FE"= IntentionEducMigActFE,
#"Intention to use ECS by Income level of the mother with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"      = IntentionIncome,
#"Intention to use ECS by households income with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"      = IntentionIncomeFm,
#"Intention to use ECS by education level (ordered) with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"      = IntentionEduc  ,
"Intention to use ECS with interaction EducXMig"      = IntentionEducXMig,
"Intention to use ECS with interaction EducXMig with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"      = IntentionEducXMigFE, 
"Intention to use ECS with interaction EducXMig controlling for activity with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"      = IntentionEducXMigActFE

   ), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs", "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: WardxWave"),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Intention to use ECS, education level, and migration background",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE)

```

There is still an effect of the level of education, even when controlling for migration background. The interaction between mothers' level of education and migration background is significant. However, when we control for whether the mother is active, the effect of migration background disappears. When we both introduce the interaction term and activity, it is the effect of education level that disappears (*how to interpret that?*).

```{r, fig.cap="Interaction plot between Education level and migration background of the mother"}

fittedmod <- glm(as.numeric(Intention1or0 ) ~ Educ*FrenchYN, data = data_full)

cat_plot(fittedmod, pred = Educ, modx = FrenchYN, geom = "line")

```

```{r, fig.cap="Interaction plot between Education level and migration background of the mother controlling for activity"}

fittedmod <- glm(as.numeric(Intention1or0 ) ~ Educ*FrenchYN + Active, data = data_full)

cat_plot(fittedmod, pred = Educ, modx = FrenchYN, geom = "line")

```

### Level of income

We nearly have a linear relationship between income during pregnancy and intention to use ECS after birth:

```{r, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE, fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by income of the mother"}

  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x=Income),position="stack",alpha=.2)+

```

This relationship is not exactly the same for family income as there seems to be more a U shaped story: when family income is very low, mothers are incentivized to work and thus want to use ECS. It is not the same for household around minimum wage that may be more in a position to afford a traditional family model.

This raises the question of whether mothers' activity is predicted by level of education and migration. The results of the OLS indicates that mothers' level of education and migration background both predict whether mothers are active or not, but the interaction between the two is not significant.

```{r ModActive, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}

ActiveEduc         <- feols( Active1or0 ~ Educ , data = data_full) 
ActiveEducFE       <- feols( Active1or0 ~ Educ | blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave) 
ActiveMig          <- feols( Active1or0 ~  FrenchYN , data = data_full)
ActiveMigFE        <- feols( Active1or0 ~  FrenchYN | blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave)  
ActiveEducXMigFE   <- feols( Active1or0 ~ Educ + FrenchYN +  Educ*FrenchYN| blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave)  
 

 modelsummary(list(
"Predicted activity by Educ level"                                                = ActiveEduc, 
"Predicted activity by Educ level with FE"                                        = ActiveEducFE,
"Predicted activity by Migrant background"                                        = ActiveMig,
"Predicted activity by Migrant background with FE"                                = ActiveMigFE,
"Activity with interaction EducXMig with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"      = ActiveEducXMigFE

   ), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",

```

## Timing of ECS wanted

```{r }

library(data.table)

# Convert data_full to a data.table
setDT(data_full)

# Create an empty binary variable
data_full[, ECSDateBinary := NA_character_]

# Define the cutoff date
cutoff_date <- as.Date("2023-09-02")

# Set values for ECS dates before and after the cutoff
data_full[ECSDate < cutoff_date, ECSDateBinary := "Before 09.2023"]
data_full[ECSDate >= cutoff_date, ECSDateBinary := "After 09.2023"]


chisq.test(data_full$Educ, data_full$ECSDateBinary)


```

High-SES mothers tend to put their child significantly earlier in ECS (X-squared = 16.377, df = 1, p-value = 5.191e-05). For instance, `r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup" & ECSDateBinary == "Before 09.2023") %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup") %>% nrow(), digit = 1)*100`% of high-SES mothers want to put their child in ECS in September 2023 or before, while it is the case for only `r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" & ECSDateBinary == "Before 09.2023") %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow(), digit = 1)*100`% low-SES mothers. Of course, this decision is likely to have heavy consequences for an effective access to ECS as most of the places are allocated around June for September.

## Type of childcare wanted

Among parents wanting to use an ECS, those wanting *crèches* (daycare centers) are over-represented: `r round(data_full %>% filter(ECSPlanTo == TRUE & WantCreche == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % want to use them (`r round(data_full %>% filter( WantCreche == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % on the general population).

```{r}
   

data_full %>% 
  filter(ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% 
ggplot(aes(ECSType7, fill = ECSType7), colour = cbPalette)+
  geom_bar()+
  labs( x = "Type of early childcare wanted for the child", fill = "")+
coord_flip()


```

### Analysis for low-SES

Again, the pattern is quite similar if we restrict the analyses to low-SES mothers: `r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" &  WantCreche == TRUE & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE ) %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % want to use daycare. The same holds for migrant families: `r round(data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else" &  WantCreche == TRUE & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE ) %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % want to use them. Even more interestingly, even among inactive parents, the proportion wanting to use daycare is still quite high and the pattern is the same: `r  round(data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive" &  WantCreche == TRUE & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE ) %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` %. Only the drop-in daycare (halte-garderies) has a slightly higher proportion compared to the general population, but the increase is very modest: `r round((data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive" & WantHG == TRUE & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() *100 ) - (data_full %>% filter(WantHG == TRUE & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow()*100), digit = 1)` percentage points.

```{r, fig.width = 40, fig.height = 30}

   
data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive") %>% 
ggplot(aes(ECSType7, fill = ECSType7), colour = cbPalette)+
  geom_bar()+
  labs( x = "Type of early childcare wanted for the child for inactive mothers", fill = "", size = 20)+ theme(text=element_text(size=50))


```

This raises the question of the types of ECS than are known by mothers. Maybe crèches is the only structure they know of.

# Part {-}: Information dynamics

## Number of ECS known

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# Mean number of ECS known for the general population 
 meanECSKnownTotalPop = round(mean(data_full$KnownNbTypeECS), 2)

# Mean for high-SES
meanECSKnownHighSES = round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup") %>%  summarize( MeanECSKnownLowSES = mean(KnownNbTypeECS)), 1) 

# Mean for low-SES
meanECSKnownLowSES = round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>%  summarize( MeanECSKnownLowSES = mean(KnownNbTypeECS)), 1) 


# Mean for migrant
meanECSKnownMigrant = round(data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else") %>%  summarize( MeanECSKnownMig = mean(KnownNbTypeECS)), 1)

# Mean for Non Mig
meanECSKnownNonMig = round(data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "French") %>%  summarize( MeanECSKnownNonMigr = mean(KnownNbTypeECS)),1)


# Mean for inactive
meanECSKnownInactive = round(data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive") %>%  summarize( MeanECSKnownInactive = mean(KnownNbTypeECS)),1)

# Mean for Active mothers
meanECSKnownActive = round(data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Active") %>%  summarize( MeanECSKnownActiv = mean(KnownNbTypeECS)), 1)



```

First, low-SES mothers knew on average significantly less ECS types than their more affluent counterparts. When asked to tell us all the ECS type they knew, mothers knew `r meanECSKnownTotalPop` ECS types on average. But while high-SES mothers knew on average `r meanECSKnownHighSES` ECS types, low-SES mothers knew on average `r meanECSKnownLowSES` of them (t = -13.2, p-value \< 2.2e-16).

This is even more true for migrants mothers that knew `r meanECSKnownMigrant` ECS types on average regardless of their socio-economic background (t = -18.845, p-value \< 2.2e-16) and for inactive mothers (M inactive = `r meanECSKnownInactive`). This effect is still significant after controlling for activity and education level. Therefore, while migration background doesn't seem to affect ECS intention much, it may play a significant role in information dynamics.

```{r tbleNumberECSKnownSES, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}

   ), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
```

## Cost of crèche

```{r, echo = FALSE}

# Proportion of ppl not knowing at all the cost of ECS (= answering "don't know" when asked) on the general population   
CostNSP = round((data_full %>% filter(AffordCostDK == TRUE) %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>% nrow())*100, 1)

# Proportion of ppl not knowing at all the cost of ECS (= answering "don't know" when asked) among ppl that have never used ECS

# Proportion of Low-SES ppl not knowing at all the cost of ECS (= answering "don't know" when asked) among ppl that have never used ECS
PropNSPCostLow = round((data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" & ECSUsed == "Non" & AffordCostDK == TRUE) %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>%  filter(Educ == "Bac" & ECSUsed == "Non") %>% nrow())*100, 1)

# Proportion of High-SES ppl not knowing at all the cost of ECS (= answering "don't know" when asked) among ppl that have never used ECS
PropNSPCostHigh =round((data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup" & ECSUsed == "Non" & AffordCostDK == TRUE) %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>%  filter(Educ == "Sup" & ECSUsed == "Non") %>% nrow())*100, 1)



```

Relatively few people had an idea of what the cost of childcare is (regardless of whether this idea is accurate or not): `` `r CostNSP` ``% of parents couldn't tell us anything about the price of childcare (`` `r CostNSPNU` ``% of parents that have never used ECS). Low-SES mothers were significantly less likely to have an idea of the costs of a place, even if we restrict the analyses only to the ones that have never used ECS: the proportion were `` `r PropNSPCostLow` ``% for low-SES mothers, compared to `` `r PropNSPCostHigh` ``% for high-SES mothers.

### Relationship between having no idea of ECS costs and intention to use ECS

Going back to our qualitative evidence, we saw that not knowing the cost of childcare can have asymmetrical consequences depending on socioeconomic status. While high-SES families are confident they can afford the cost, no matter what it is (or nearly), low-SES families will be more reluctant to apply because they "cannot end up with another bill they cannot pay".

Running the regressions (see \@ref(Appendix 3) for the detailed regression table), we see that there is a significant negative impact of no knowing the costs on ECS intention (p\< 0.0005), even after controlling for Education level, Migration background, and Activity. As expected given the figures below, none of the interactions with migration background nor education level is significant.

```{r,  LinearSubsidies,echo = FALSE}
KnowsSubsidiesEducFE    <-feols(AffordSubsidies1or0 ~ Educ | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave) 
KnowsSubsidiesMig     <-feols(AffordSubsidies1or0 ~ FrenchYN | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
KnowsSubsidiesEducMig <-feols(AffordSubsidies1or0 ~ Educ + FrenchYN| blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
KnowsSubsidiesEducUsed<-feols(AffordSubsidies1or0 ~ Educ + ECSUsed | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
KnowsSubsidiesMigUsed <-feols(AffordSubsidies1or0 ~ FrenchYN + ECSUsed | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
KnowsSubsidiesEducXMig<-feols(AffordSubsidies1or0 ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Educ*FrenchYN| blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)


modelsummary(list(
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies by Educ" = KnowsSubsidiesEduc,  
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies by Educ with FE" = KnowsSubsidiesEducFE,  
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies by Mig" = KnowsSubsidiesMig,   
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies by Educ and Mig" = KnowsSubsidiesEducMig, 
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies by Educ and ever used" = KnowsSubsidiesEducUsed,
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies by mig and ever used " = KnowsSubsidiesMigUsed, 
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies EducXMig " = KnowsSubsidiesEducXMig
), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs", "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: WardxWave" ),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Probability to know that the price of crèche is reduced through subsidies",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE)


```

### Relationship between knowing that ECS cost is reduced through subsidies and intention to use ECS

Running the regressions (see \@ref(Appendix 4) for the detailed regression table), we see that there is a significant negative impact of not knowing that ECS cost is reduced through subsidies on ECS intention (p\< 0.0005), even after controlling for Education level, Migration background, and Activity. While the interaction between not knowing about the subsidies and migration background is not significant, the one with education level is.

```{r GraphIntentionSubsidiesEduc, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE, fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by number of ECS known"}

  stat_summary(aes(x = as.factor(AffordSubsidies1or0), y = Intention1or0*1000) ,

               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975)),
```

```{r dataset2}
           "Assignment", "Which_wave", "labels", "blocksMatWaveStrata", "blocksMatWave", "code_commune", "code_departement"
           
)

data_full[,names] <- lapply(data_full[,names] , factor)

#convert relevant VARIABLES INTO numerical ones


names_numerical <- c("AgeChild1", "AgeChild2", "AgeChild3", "AgeChild4", "AgeChild5", "AgeChild6", "AgeChild7", "AgeChild8",
                     "Age", "KnowsCreche", "KnowsCrecheA", "KnowsCrechePub", "KnowsAssMat", "KnowsNotYet", "KnowsJE", "KnowsAutre",

                     "WantAutre", "WantPartage", "WantHG", "WantNounou", "KnownNbTypeECS", "PregMonth", "BreastFeedLength",
                     "BreastFeedIntend1or0", "AffordSubsidies1or0", "NormsOpposedN", "LikertReturnHK1or0", "TrustCreche1or0",
                     "AffordCost", "NumberChildren", "AccessImpossible", "AccessHard", "AccessHardtoImpossible", "AccessEasy1or0",

                     "TAUXCOUV_COM", "TAUXCOUV_EPCI", "TAUXCOUV_DEP", "TAUXCOUV_NAT", "n", "strata", "group_id", "prixMoyen", 
                     "PrixMedian", "surfaceReelleBati", "PrixMoyenM2Bati")
data_full[,names_numerical] <- lapply(data_full[,names_numerical] , as.numeric)

# Order relevant variables


data_full <- data_full %>%  mutate(
         OrderedEduc=factor(OrderedEduc, levels =
             c("No school", "9-11", "Brevet", "CAP", "Bac", "Bac +2", "Bac + 3", "Bac + 4/5", "+ Bac+5"), ordered = TRUE),
         Income = factor(Income, 
                         levels = c("NSP","- 500","500-700", "1000-1500", 
                                    "1500-2000", "2000-2500", "2500-3000", "3000-4500", "4500-5000",  "5000-6000", "Ne veut pas répondre" ), ordered = TRUE),
         FmlyIncome = factor(FmlyIncome, 
                             levels =c("NSP", "- 500", "500-700", "700-1000", "1000-1500", 
                                       "1500-2000", "2000-2500", "2500-3000", "3000-4500", "4500-5000",
                                       "5000-6000", "6000-7000", "7000-8000", "+8000", "Ne veut pas répondre"), ordered = TRUE),
          AffordNMCostWBOrdered=factor(AffordNMCostWB,
                               levels=c("Négatif",  "Je ne sais pas encore","Pas d'impact","Positif"), ordered = TRUE # would staying at home have a positive, 
         ),                                                                   # negative or null impact on mother's well being
         AffordOppCost=factor(AffordOppCost,
                              levels=c("Négatif",  "Je ne sais pas encore", "Pas d'impact", "Positif"), ordered = TRUE # would staying at home have a positive, 
         ),                                                                   # negative or null impact on household's income
         AffordNMCostCareer=factor(AffordNMCostCareer, # would staying at home have a positive, 
                                   levels=c("Négatif", "Pas d'impact", "Je ne sais pas encore","Positif"), ordered = TRUE # negative or null impact on mother's career
         ),
         AccessEasy=factor(AccessEasy,levels =c("impossible","quasiment impossible", # Whether accessing a slot in ECS is seen as easy
                                                   "très difficile","assez difficile",
                                                   "je ne sais pas","assez facile",
                                                   "très facile"),ordered = TRUE), 
         AccessHours=factor(AccessHours,levels =c("Oui", # Whether ECS opening hours fit parents working hours
                                                     "Non, mais on prendra un autre mode de garde en plus","Je ne sais pas encore",
                                                     "Non"),ordered = TRUE),
         AccessInformalCare=factor(AccessInformalCare,levels =c("Oui, autant que nécessaire", # Whether accessing informal care is feasible
                                                          "Oui, de temps en temps","Oui, pour dépanner / très ponctuellement",
                                                          "Je ne sais pas encore",
                                                          "Non"),ordered = TRUE),
         Norms=factor(Norms,
                      levels=c("Ne sait pas","Aucune","Une minorité","Moitié moitié","La plupart","Toutes"), ordered = TRUE # how many mothers in their surroundings use childcare 
         ),
     LikertAccessInfo=factor(LikertAccessInfo, # Is it feasible to access information about childcare
                            levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord"), ordered = TRUE), # strongly disagree, disagree, don't know, agree, strongly agree
    LikertReturnHK=factor(LikertReturnHK, # believe in childcare returns on investment: is a child that attended childcare better developed in preschool?
                          levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord") , ordered = TRUE), # strongly disagree, disagree, don't know, agree, strongly agree
    LikertAccessSoc=factor(LikertAccessSoc, # Does the mother have someone that can help with paperwork if needed
                           levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord"), ordered = TRUE), # strongly disagree, disagree, don't know, agree, strongly agree
    TrustFam=factor(TrustFam, # TRUST: Do the parents trust their close family (parents, brother, sister, etc.) to take care of the baby
                    levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord"),  ordered = TRUE
    ),
    TrustFriend=factor(TrustFriend, # TRUST: Do the parents trust their friends to take care of the baby
                       levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord"), ordered = TRUE
    ),
    TrustAssMat=factor(TrustAssMat, # TRUST: Do the parents trust a private childminder to take care of the baby
                       levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord"), ordered = TRUE
    ),
    TrustCreche=factor(TrustCreche, # TRUST: Do the parents trust their family to take care of the baby
                       levels=c("Très en désaccord","Assez en désaccord","Je ne sais pas","Assez d’accord","Très d’accord"), ordered = TRUE
    ),
    DeprivClothes =factor(DeprivClothes,levels=c("Pas du tout","Un peu","Beaucoup","Je ne souhaite pas répondre"), ordered = TRUE), # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to buy clothes?
    DeprivFood    =factor(DeprivFood,levels=c("Pas du tout","Un peu","Beaucoup","Je ne souhaite pas répondre"), ordered = TRUE), # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to buy food?
    DeprivBills   =factor(DeprivBills,levels=c("Pas du tout","Un peu","Beaucoup","Je ne souhaite pas répondre"), ordered = TRUE), # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to pay for the bills?
    DeprivHolidays=factor(DeprivHolidays,levels=c("Pas du tout","Un peu","Beaucoup","Je ne souhaite pas répondre"), ordered = TRUE), # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to go in holidays?
    DeprivHousing =factor(DeprivHousing,levels=c("Pas du tout","Un peu","Beaucoup","Je ne souhaite pas répondre"), ordered = TRUE), # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to pay for housing?
    InformalReciprocity = factor(InformalReciprocity, 
                                 levels = c( "Non", " Je ne souhaite pas répondre", "Oui, pour dépanner / très ponctuellement",
                                              "Oui, de temps en temps", " Oui, très souvent"), ordered = TRUE), # Do the parents already take care of the children of others
OrderedEduc2=factor(OrderedEduc2, levels  = c(
  "No school", "9-11", "Brevet", "CAP", "Bac", "Bac +2", "Bac + 3", "Bac + 4/5", "+ Bac+5","Missing","No Partner"), ordered = TRUE),
ECSIdealAgeEntry = factor(ECSIdealAgeEntry, 
                          levels = c( "Ne sait pas", "Jamais", "Pendant ses trois premiers mois", "Pendant ses six premiers mois", "Pendant ses neuf premiers mois", "Pendant la première année", "Jusqu’à l’entrée à la maternelle" ) , ordered = TRUE), 
Active = ifelse(as.character(Act3) == "NSP", "Inactive", as.character(Act3)), 
Active = relevel(as.factor(Active), ref = "Inactive"), 
Active1or0 = ifelse(as.character(Active) == "Inactive", 0, 1),
Educ3 = fct_collapse(OrderedEduc, "Bac or Less" = c("No school", "9-11", "Brevet", "CAP", "Bac"), 
                    "Undergrad" = c("Bac + 3", "Bac +2"), 
                    "Graduate" = c("Bac + 4/5", "+ Bac+5") ), 
Educ3Dad = fct_collapse(OrderedEduc2, "Bac or Less" = c("No school", "9-11", "Brevet", "CAP", "Bac"), 
                    "Undergrad" = c("Bac + 3", "Bac +2"), 
                    "Graduate" = c("Bac + 4/5", "+ Bac+5"), "Missing" = c("Missing", "No Partner" )), 
Intention1or0 = ifelse(as.character(Intention.x) == "No", 0, 1)

)
```

## Appendix 1 {-}: Regression table of the relationship between Number of ECS known and Intention {#id}

```{r modIntentionNECSKnown,echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}

# Relationship between Number of ECS known and Intention


IntentionECSKnown            <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ KnownNbTypeECS, data = data_full)
IntentionECSKnownFE          <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ KnownNbTypeECS| blocksMatWave , data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)

IntentionECSKnownEducMigAct  <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ KnownNbTypeECS + Educ + FrenchYN + Active| blocksMatWave , data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave )

), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
```

Not only low-SES mothers knew less ECS types than high-SES mothers did, but low-SES mothers were significantly more likely to know Crèches and only Crèches (low-SES \= `` `r PropKnowOnlyCrecheLowSES` `` , high-SES = `` `r PropKnowOnlyCrecheHighSES` `` ). This is also true for migrant mothers, that were even more likely to be in this situation than low-SES mothers ( migrants \= `` `r PropKnowOnlyCrecheMig` `` ), while only `` `r PropKnowOnlyCrecheNonMig` `` percents of native mothers were in this situation.


Strikingly, it was also the case for inactive mothers: `` `r PropKnowOnlyCrecheInactive` `` percents of them only knew the crèches, while it was the case for `` `r PropKnowOnlyCrecheActive` ``percents of active mothers. This even though generally, inactive mothers are less likely to access a place in crèche because they don't work. Besides, inactive mothers are just as likely to know Halte-garderies compared to active mothers. Only `` `r PropKnowHGInactive` `` percents of them knew this type of structure, while this is one type of care created for them.

Interestingly, looking at the coefficients of the regressions, whether the mother is active is contributing to a lesser extent than Education level and Migration background, unlike its contribution to ECS intention:

2.  Grouped in three groups
